title: Nana: Why the 20 year old anime is still breaking the internet
body: Two decades after it first aired, Nana continues to rack up new fans discovering it for the first time, and old fans returning to it with fresh eyes.
Its unflinching look at friendship, ambition, and heartbreak set it apart from the shonen-dominated anime landscape of its era, and that honesty still lands today.
Whether it's the soundtrack, the fashion, or Nana Osaki's unapologetic edge, the series keeps finding new audiences one recommendation at a time.

title: FC 27: Kylian Mbappe Always Breaks the Internet
body: Every new FC release, one name dominates the conversation before the game even launches: Kylian Mbappé.
This year's cover star comes with new pace stats and a rebuilt dribbling engine that's already splitting opinion among competitive players.
Whether you love or hate the meta he creates, there's no denying his presence shapes how the whole community plays the game.

title: 2026; BTS' regrouping
body: After years apart on individual projects and service commitments, BTS's full regrouping in 2026 has sent ARMY into a frenzy.
Early previews suggest a sound that blends each member's solo growth with the group chemistry that made them global icons in the first place.
Ticket demand for the reunion tour has already broken records before a single date was confirmed.

title: Big Names That Starred in The Odyssey
body: Christopher Nolan's take on Homer's epic assembled one of the most stacked casts in recent memory.
From seasoned veterans to breakout newcomers, every role was cast with an eye for gravity and screen presence.
The result is a film that critics are already calling a career-defining moment for more than one actor on the call sheet.

title: Netflix's Arcane is still talked about two years after it's finale
body: Two years since its finale aired, Arcane's fandom shows no signs of slowing down.
Its animation style redefined what a game adaptation could look like, and its willingness to let characters suffer real consequences kept audiences talking long after the credits rolled.
Fan theories, art, and rewatch threads still surface daily, cementing its place as one of the most influential animated series of its generation.

title: Iyanu; Nigeria's first comic
body: Iyanu has become a landmark moment for African representation in comics, drawing on Yoruba mythology for a story that feels both ancient and entirely new.
Its adaptation into animation introduced the character to a global audience, but the source material remains a favorite among longtime readers.
The series continues to open doors for more homegrown stories to reach international shelves.

title: The Manga Breaking the Internet: Kagurabachi
body: Kagurabachi's explosive rise has drawn comparisons to some of the biggest names in shonen history, and it's easy to see why.
Its sharp art style and brutal sword-fighting sequences have made it a favorite for panel-by-panel breakdowns online.
With each new chapter breaking engagement records, it's quickly becoming the manga to watch this generation.
